title: Owner decision: how a surviving hand mutant counts for convergence, and a code-freeze window for two clean rounds (the SHIP blocker)
description:
WHY THIS IS THE SHIP BLOCKER. The README's verdict is HOLD because scripts/converge.sh needs the last two non-author rounds clean (T2 rule, fewer than three genuine findings each). Rounds 6-19 are all not clean. Evidence gathered in the 2026-09-23 reality check (session ef481f9c): since round 9 NO round has found a conversion difference from the pinned original (rounds 18 and 19: about 607,000 and 1,090,000 compared executions, 0 differences; the corpus is 1076/1076 on four lanes); every BEHAVIOR finding of rounds 17-19 (R17-1, R18-1..5, R19-1..4) is a hand-written MUTANT that survives the corpus and the proof because no law pins that corner; the remaining findings are DOCUMENT findings. Two structural facts make the counter unable to reach 2: (1) any def can be mutated, so a reviewer who writes new mutants in defs no law names will always find survivors; (2) every merged performance lever adds new code for the next round to mutate (EXP-025..032 landed between rounds 18 and 20).

THE DECISION (owner's; raised first as R15-1 on 2026-09-22, still pending in docs/PORT_STATE.md 'Owner decisions'):
(a) STRICT: a surviving mutant stays a behavior finding. Then SHIP needs a CODE FREEZE: no port/ change except repairs for two consecutive non-author rounds; perf levers accumulate on a branch and land after certification, each re-opening the gate.
(b) CLASSED: a surviving mutant is a LAW-COVERAGE finding in its own column (like document findings: it blocks SHIP only if unrepaired, but does not reset the clean counter); a behavior finding is a byte/exit/proof difference against the original or a broken gate. Then rounds 18 and 19 would already have 0 behavior findings.
(c) BOTH: classed counting AND a freeze for the two certifying rounds.
Recommendation of the author: (c). It keeps mutation testing as a quality driver (every survivor still gets a law) while making the gate terminate, and the freeze removes the 'moving target'.

AFTER THE DECISION: record it in docs/PORT_STATE.md 'Owner decisions' and in the porting-to-bend2 skill's PARITY-GATE 'Counting findings' (converge.sh reads the rounds table; a new column may be needed), then run round 20 and 21 on the frozen tree (brief template: session scratchpad round20-prompt.md; targets EXP-029..032 and the round-19 repairs). Acceptance: converge.sh prints CONVERGED, or the owner's written choice is recorded with the reason it is not.

Decided (c), recorded in docs/PORT_STATE.md 'Owner decisions' (work21, lands with toon_bend-g15): from round 20 the rounds table's 'new genuine findings' counts BEHAVIOR findings only (a difference from the original, a wrong proof verdict, a lying gate); a surviving hand mutant is a LAW-COVERAGE finding and a refuted claim a DOCUMENT finding, both repaired before SHIP, neither making a round unclean. title: Perf: String and Json are hot (refcounted) types; borrow inference lends 2 of 496 segments, so every read takes shared values apart (term_drop/span_fade 35-45% of decode)
description: Found 2026-09-22 (session ef481f9c) with ~/.claude/skills/bend2-mega-skill/scripts/keep-audit.sh on port/main.bend at the tree of 5331d3e: 496 segments, peek 2, keep 361, take 338. gprof of gsoc_2018 --decode after EXP-009/011: term_drop 35-42% flat, span_fade 36-47% inclusive; encode of twitter/citm: String.reverse 15-25% (JSON reader tokens, line assembly). Heat is per TYPE: one owned use of a String followed by another (e.g. a key stored in the key set T.KT and in its entry) makes every String cell counted. Levers, each needs a card: (1) key sets that store key HASHES plus a pointer-free comparison, so no String is stored twice; (2) readers that only match (is_nil, all_prim, all_obj, row.lock) with no escape anywhere downstream, so borrow inference can lend; (3) a packed string representation (U32 array chunks) for keys and values - a carrier change across text/json/encode/decode. NE-012 (BN.cmp) and NE-014 (trim_end) are the two measured edges of this problem.

comments.text: 2026-09-24 profile (EXP-031 code, frame-pointer tally of rfc_wrap, gsoc_2018.fold.toon --decode --expand-paths safe, the most expensive scenario per byte in a4's reference run): 23.7M list cells for 2.9 MB, ~8 per input byte, spread over reading the file (1/byte, IO), the UTF-8 text (1/byte), the scanner (1/byte), string literal decoding (2/byte: DECODE_LIT_GO builds and reverses) and the JSON writer (2 per output byte, reversed build + one reverse). So the next large perf step is this bead's representation change (packed strings / not holding the tree twice), not another list lever; it should start after convergence, not during the freeze.

title: COUNTED noise floor: measure how much a constructor-table shift alone moves cachegrind counts, before trusting any counted delta under ~2%
description:
FINDING (2026-09-23, NE-036): EXP-032 changed only the ENCODE arm (two new types RU/RR and four defs in json.bend), yet four DECODE cells whose Bend code is identical counted +1.04% to +1.84% against the EXP-031 binary (semanticscholar.toon 11,286,330,337 -> 11,492,568,790; twitter.toon, citm_catalog.toon, openapi_github.toon likewise). The emitted C's constructor table (CID numbering, CID_ARITY_T) changes whenever a type is added, and with it dispatch code layout. EXP-031's own encode 'regression' (gsoc +0.80%, NE-035) may be the same effect. So COUNTED is deterministic run-to-run (~1e-8) but NOT build-to-build: an unrelated edit can move a cell by up to ~2%. Every counted gate below that size (EXP-029's canada allowance 0.5%, EXP-031/032's 0.5% guards, NE-017's 2.98% vs 3%) is currently judged without knowing the floor.

METHOD: build A/A pairs of the SAME port semantics that differ only in (1) one unused Data type added at the top of json.bend, (2) one unused type at the bottom of main.bend, (3) one unused def; count all 12 cells of the 2c33e64 table plus the four out-of-sample decode cells for each; report per-cell spread (max |delta|) as the floor. Then cg_annotate the largest mover to name the mechanism (switch table, inlining, register allocation). DELIVERABLE: one line in perf/NEGATIVE-EVIDENCE.md's preamble and in the porting skill's PERFORMANCE-CAMPAIGN: 'a counted delta between builds is attributable only above <floor>% or with a per-function comparison'; re-judge NE-035/NE-036's guard failures against it (they may be noise, which would make both levers clean wins). Acceptance: the floor number with its A/A evidence files in perf/evidence/.
close_reason: Mechanism identified instead of a synthetic A/A floor (an unused type may not even be emitted, so an A/A build could show 0 and prove nothing): per-function cachegrind comparison of twitter.toon --decode, EXP-031 vs EXP-032 binaries (identical Bend decode code): WL_FID_CLI_CONVERT 0 -> 34,266,888 (the UTF-8 walk spin_499 inlined into the worklist function), spin totals 207,411,715 -> 185,412,913; net +12.3M of the cell's +12,982,156 (+1.84%). The opposite direction on gsoc encode between d5483e5 and EXP-031 (163.1M inlined vs 186.4M as a spin). Rule written into perf/NEGATIVE-EVIDENCE.md's preamble (work20 commit after 501f0e6): counted deltas under ~2% between builds need a per-function comparison before they are attributed. NE-035/036's guard failures are this effect.

comments.text:
EVIDENCE ATTACHED 2026-09-24 (session 9e91730b). NE-033 localised the port's worst cost to exactly this def's territory, so this candidate is now the best-evidenced unbuilt printer lever.

THE PRIZE, counted (cachegrind, deterministic). canada.json is the worst cell of the counted corpus comparison at 13.33x the original's instructions, 4,893 per input byte against 367, where every other document sits between 3.85x and 9.72x. Three twins of it, same shape and same number COUNT, different number TEXT:

  short integers       17,015 instructions per number    3.25x vs the oracle
  short decimals       62,294 per number                11.80x
  canada as published  99,121 per number                13.33x

The oracle is nearly flat across all three (582M, 587M, 827M I-refs). The port is not, and the jump is NOT the digit count: a 7-character decimal carries ~5 significant digits, well inside token.short's 14-digit bound, and already costs 11.80x. What changes between row 1 and row 2 is the presence of a FRACTION.

WHICH HALF, bisected before building (the discipline NE-033 cost me). Forcing EXP-012's scalar digit loop off separates reader from printer:

  short integers   EXP-012 ON 1,890,963,922   OFF 1,890,963,917   IDENTICAL
  short decimals   EXP-012 ON 6,922,497,426   OFF 13,448,869,374  the loop IS the cost

Integers never reach the shortest-digit generator at all (EXP-001 prints their digits directly). Decimals must, and EXP-012 already halves that. So the remaining gap is shortest-digit GENERATION for non-integers, and the READER is about 1% of it — I built the reader half as EXP-028 and it returned -0.7% against a 25% gate (NE-033, not merged).

WHY THIS BEAD'S IDEA IS THE RIGHT SHAPE. 'Reuse a short decimal's own digits' does not make generation cheaper; it SKIPS generation when the literal's own digits already round-trip, which is the pass-elimination shape that has actually paid here (NE-027's rule: eliminate a pass over the data, not an operation within one). EXP-007's JRaw already carries the original token through to the emitter, so the digits are in hand.

THE TRAP to write into the card: the literal's digits are the shortest round-tripping form only when they round-trip AND are minimal. '1.10' round-trips but is not shortest; 0.1 is not representable. The check must be exact or the goldens diverge on the first tie, and the existing closed laws on the printer's boundary values are the floor, not the ceiling.

ALTERNATIVE PATH, tracked separately: a Ryu/Grisu-class fixed-point generator with precomputed powers, replacing Burger and Dybvig's big-natural iteration. Larger, with real rounding risk; this bead's idea is the cheaper of the two and should be tried first.

title: Perf (largest remaining, number path): replace Burger-Dybvig big-natural digit generation with a Ryu/Grisu-class fixed-point method

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
WHY THIS EXISTS. NE-033 (2026-09-24) bounded the port's worst path and named this as the only remaining lever of size on it, but the conclusion lived only in a retry predicate. Tracking it so it is not rediscovered by building the wrong half again.

THE EVIDENCE. canada.json is the worst cell of the counted corpus comparison: 13.33x the original's instructions, 4,893 per input byte against 367, where every other document is between 3.85x and 9.72x. The cause is shortest-digit generation for NON-INTEGERS, isolated by three twins of the document with the same shape and number count:

  short integers  17,015 instructions per number   (never reach the generator; EXP-001 prints digits directly)
  short decimals  62,294 per number                (must generate; EXP-012 already halves this)
  canada          99,121 per number

and confirmed by forcing EXP-012's scalar loop off: integers 1,890,963,922 -> 1,890,963,917 (identical), decimals 6,922,497,426 -> 13,448,869,374.

SO: Burger and Dybvig over big naturals is the algorithm, EXP-012's U32-word loop is the obvious win already taken, and the rest needs a different algorithm rather than a fast path or a guard.

SCOPE AND RISK, stated honestly because this is not a small lever. A Ryu- or Grisu-class method replaces iteration over big naturals with fixed-point arithmetic over precomputed powers of ten. It is a substantial piece of work in the most law-protected file in the port (f64.bend), and correct rounding is the whole contract: the goldens diverge on the first tie if it is wrong, and 'ties to even' for TOON plus JavaScript's number text for JSON are both reproduced bit for bit today.

PREREQUISITES before anyone starts:
1. toon_bend-p47 first. 'Reuse a short decimal's own digits when printing' SKIPS generation for the common case and is far cheaper to build and to prove. If it lands, the remaining prize here shrinks and may not justify the risk. This bead is the fallback, not the first move.
2. A quantified fast==spec law is not available for this path (NE-001: the checker's normalizer overflows on bodies with 10^5-scale Nat literals), so the binding would be closed laws through F.bits plus the million-number differential plus the kill switch — the same ladder the existing twins use, and the claim must say which rung it reached.
3. Gate it on ALL FOUR LANES before it lands, not c-1t alone: EXP-032 type-checked, proved and passed 1076 cases on c-1t, then aborted two cases on js and the interpreter because the C runtime does not check that a Char holds a Unicode scalar value and the other two do (NE-036). Anything touching the number path's traversal shape or error order inherits that risk.
4. Precommit the gate in COUNTED terms (instructions), since wall-clock captures on this host have been refused for days, and state the tree by its BINARY sha256 rather than its commit.

title: Nested repeated-key merge is still quadratic: one key repeated n times whose object grows (4000: 2.7 s vs the original's 0.04 s)
description:
Follow-up to toon_bend-qgu, which fixed the OUTER chain (n distinct keys each repeated: 2.51 s ->
0.08 s at n=2000, linear again). The nested case is untouched: a document of n lines 'a:' each
carrying a distinct inner key makes the merge target object grow, and dup.merge still calls dups()
over that chain, so each occurrence costs O(i). Measured 2026-09-22 on the fix (8 cores): grow1000
0.15 s, grow2000 0.73 s, grow4000 2.72 s (before the fix: 0.16 / 0.74 / 2.45); the original does
4000 in 0.04 s. A fix needs the value tree itself to stay map-backed while an object is open (the km
of a merged child would have to persist across occurrences), which is a carrier change one level
deeper than qgu; EXP-004's precedent applies. diff-fuzz scale passes today because its 'every key
repeated' input is the outer shape, so add a lens input of the nested shape with the fix.

DESIGN NOTES (2026-09-22, from the qgu fix session; do not re-derive):
1. Why qgu's fix does not reach this: the frame's J.KM makes the OUTER object's lookup/update O(log), but a
   repeated key whose value is an object still merges through dups() over the STORED inner chain, which grows.
2. Three designs were considered.
   (a) HOT CHILD: the frame caches (key, inner chain reversed, inner KM) for the LAST merged key; consecutive
       repeats become O(1) amortised, a key switch flushes (O(i), today's cost, no regression). Fixes the lens
       input and the common shape; a repeat one level deeper is still quadratic. ~4 frame fields + flush logic.
   (b) MAP-BACKED VALUE TREE (general): the decoder builds objects as MV{chain, KM-of-MV} and materialises
       J.Json at close. Fixes every depth. Needs a KM whose values are MV (the current KM is monomorphic over
       Json), so ~40 lines of carrier plus every object-construction site in decode.bend.
   (c) DEFER the merge to the parent's close: rejected. The merge would stop happening in attach order, and the
       first 'Duplicate sibling key' failure is reported by document position; an inner object closes before the
       outer object's later keys attach, so two failures in different objects could swap. It would need the
       pending duplicates to carry their line numbers and G.dup to keep the smallest, which is more machinery
       than (b) for less generality.
3. Recommended: (b). Do it when port/decode.bend is not being edited by a review round, and re-run
   diff-fuzz scale (the nested inputs are committed in 0e4f1d0 and are RED until this is fixed).
